title: Engineers Fire 4-Pound Chickens at Jet Engines on Purpose

scenes.text: Engineers fire dead chickens at jet engines on purpose.
scenes.keywords: air cannon test laboratory jet engine

scenes.text: It's real. An air cannon launches a bird carcass into an engine or windshield.
US and European rules require engines to survive a bird strike.
A modern test fires a four-pound bird at about 350 miles an hour.
scenes.keywords: high speed impact test slow motion

scenes.text: In the 1970s, one fired at a Boeing cockpit roof punched through the skin. The cockpit had to be reinforced.
Why chickens? Cheap. And never frozen, because that isn't realistic. A chicken, an air cannon, a jet engine.

description:
Aircraft makers use a compressed-air chicken gun to fire bird carcasses at engines and windshields, because certification rules require them to survive bird strikes.
A modern test launches a 4 lb bird at roughly 350 mph, and early tests on Boeing cockpit roofs showed designs that had to be reinforced.
What's the weirdest test you know of?
thumbnail_text: THEY FIRE CHICKENS AT JET ENGINES
first_comment: The chicken cannon is real, and so is the rule that engines have to pass the test before they are certified. What's the weirdest safety test you know of?
